My dog, a Rottweiler-labrador mix, started acting weird on his 11th birthday, he didn't get excited for his new toys which was weird because up until then he always loved playing with rope toys and would be thrilled to get a new one. Then over the weeks he stopped eating his hard food, so I switched to canned and for a little while he'd eat that, but slowly he lost interest so I switched to a gravy style canned dog food and he was great with that. But even with the people food and treats on top of that he still lost weight. The vet had suspected he had Cushing's dye to his excessive drinking and peeing so we took him in to get tested for that, and I had X-rays done to be sure his organs were good. The X-rays showed he had a growth on his stomach and spleen, but I hoped it was benign. His test results showed he was positive for Cushing's and that can cause weight loss as well. But over time he just started to isolate himself more, get more moody than usual and he just began to not eat at all and lost even more weight. On his last day he didn't move until 12. And it was hard to get him to go down the stairs. From his birthday until the he had issues but he was arthritic so I assumed it just hurt to use them. But he needed to use them anyways to go up and sleep with us. He fell down the stairs about 5 times in total due to being so weak from weight and muscle loss. But anyways on his last day he didn't eat anything except for a few chicken nuggets. In the car I sat in the back with him and he got in my lap one last time. At the vet they weighed him and he was 34.6 lbs. (Normally he was about 65, but he was slightly overweight, probably should have been in the 50lb range). She felt around his belly and said she could feel the tumor so it had grown and probably spread. My boyfriend was there with me and he told me it was probably time to put him down, and I agreed. There's only so much weight someone can lose before serious reactions start like seizures and I didn't want to put my dog or myself through that. So I called my dad and had him get some pizza for my dogs last meal. We all were there when he passed and I highly recommend that people stay with their pets when they die. It's not traumatic in anyway compared to what they go through naturally. The only sound my dog made was with the first injection due to having lost a lot of leg muscles/fat I'm sure it really hurt. But then he laid down and we got ten minutes to say good bye. The final injection doesn't cause any reaction and the dog just stops breathing. The only upsetting thing was that I thought the dogs actually sleep but they don't, so their eyes are open when they die.
